Main.sentence: Wycliffe K. Grousbeck (born June 13, 1961) is an American ___E:entrepreneur U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entrepreneur)___ , who was lead owner and Governor of the ___E:Boston Celtics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics)___ of the ___E:National Basketball Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association)___ from December 2002 unitl August 2025, winning 2 NBA Championships during that time. He now serves as co-lead owner and CEO of the team alongside William Chisholm.

Grousbeck was born in ___E:Worcester, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worcester,_Massachusetts)___ and graduated from ___E:Noble and Greenough School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noble_and_Greenough_School)___ in ___E:Dedham, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dedham,_Massachusetts)___ .

He attended ___E:Princeton University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princeton_University)___ , ___E:B.A. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts)___ in ___E:history U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History)___ in 1983, and rowed on the 1983 undefeated lightweight crew team that claimed the Ivy League and National rowing championship.

Grousbeck earned his ___E:J.D. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor)___ degree from the ___E:University of Michigan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Michigan_Law_School)___ in 1986 and his ___E:M.B.A. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Business_Administration)___ in 1992 (Miller Scholar) from the ___E:Stanford Graduate School of Business U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_Graduate_School_of_Business)___ .

After spending seven years as a partner at the ___E:venture capital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venture_capital)___ firm, ___E:Highland Capital Partners U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highland_Capital_Partners)___ , Grousbeck founded and led the group, ___E:Boston Basketball Partners L.L.C. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Basketball_Partners_L.L.C.)___ , that bought the ___E:Boston Celtics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics)___ for $360 million in 2002.  During his time as lead owner, the Celtics won NBA championships in ___E:2008 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_NBA_Finals)___ and ___E:2024 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals)___ .
They made the playoffs in 20 of Grousbeck's 23 years in charge.

After their second win in 2024, Grousbeck and his family revealed their intention to sell the franchise, and on August 19, 2025, he announced the closing of the sale for a record setting $6.1 billion to ___E:Bill Chisholm U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Chisholm_(businessman))___ , a managing partner of ___E:Symphony Technology Group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symphony_Technology_Group)___ .
At the closing of the sale, it was revealed that Grousbeck currently owns less than 15% of the team, which although substantial ownership does not permit him to serve as Governor under League rules.
Grousbeck is expected to remain with the Celtics until 2028, at which time he would be able to sell his shares to Chisholm at a calculated new team valuation, which may be as high as $7.3 billion.
Besides the Celtics, Grousbeck has had numerous other business ventures.

In 2010, he became Chairman of the ___E:Massachusetts Eye and Ear Infirmary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Eye_and_Ear_Infirmary)___ (MEE), a research and clinical hospital specializing in blindness and deafness research.

Grousbeck instituted and led a capital campaign that raised $250 million for MEE, and led them to join ___E:Mass General Brigham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_General_Brigham)___ medical system.

In 2013, he co-founded Causeway Media Partners, LP, a growth equity partnership managing over $330 million, investing in sports technology and media companies such as ___E:Omaze, Inc U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omaze)___ ., ___E:Zwift U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zwift)___ , ___E:FloSports U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FloSports)___ , Freeletics, the PGA Tour, and ___E:SeatGeek U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SeatGeek)___ .
Wyc has served as Executive Producer on two recent Hollywood productions.

He co-created and was an Executive Producer of the 2023 ___E:NBC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC)___ sitcom ___E:Extended Family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_Family_(TV_series))___ , loosely based on Grousbeck, his wife, and her ex-husband (a lifelong Celtics fan).

Grousbeck also appeared in, and was an Executive Producer of, the critically acclaimed ___E:HBO Sports U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO)___ documentary on the Celtics, "Celtics City" which aired on HBO Max in 2025.

Grousbeck married Emilia Fazzalari in 2017.  They joined with fellow NBA owners ___E:Michael Jordan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jordan)___ , ___E:Jeanie Buss U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanie_Buss)___ and ___E:Wes Edens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Edens)___ to found Cincoro Tequila, which launched in September 2019.
In 2022, Princeton University opened a new dormitory, Grousbeck Hall, which was funded through a donation from the Grousbeck family.
Wyc and Emilia also created the Fazzalari Sky Bridge serving Boston Children’s Hospital patients, and support the Grousbeck Boys and Girls Club of Charlestown, Mass. [citation needed]
Grousbeck is an avid rock and blues drummer and guitarist.

He has appeared on stage around Boston and New York City with his band French Lick, the Grammy nominated James Montgomery Band. He has shared bills with such headliners as Billy Idol, Gregg Allman, Lenny Kravitz, the B-52s, Flo Rida, and the J. Geils Band. [citation needed]
